Dennis & Schnabel, Numerical Methods for Unconstrained Optimization and Nonlinear Equations (1983), §6.5

name: Bracketing a minimum

params.name: step
params.help: First step: the second point is x₀ + step.

params.name: grow_limit
params.help: A parabolic extrapolation may reach at most uₗᵢₘ = b + grow_limit·(c − b) (must be > 1, so uₗᵢₘ lies beyond c).

params.name: max_iter
params.help: Iteration limit.

summary: Walk downhill with steps that grow by the golden ratio (or a parabolic jump) until f turns up: the last three points bracket a minimum.
references: Press et al., Numerical Recipes (3rd ed.), §10.1 (Bracketmethod::bracket, mnbrak)

name: Brent's method (minimization)

params.name: xtol
params.help: Absolute tolerance t: stop when x is within 2(rtol·|x| + xtol/3) of both bracket ends. f-comparisons limit the accuracy to h ≈ √ε·(1 + |x⋆|) (about 10⁻⁸).

params.name: rtol
params.help: Relative tolerance (Brent's eps; √ε by default). Below √ε the guarantee 2(rtol·|x| + xtol/3) can fail: f-comparisons resolve x⋆ only to about √ε·(1 + |x⋆|).

params.name: max_iter
params.help: Iteration limit.

order: superlinear (≈ 1.324) for smooth f; guaranteed convergence otherwise
summary: Golden-section search that switches to parabolic interpolation whenever the parabola is trustworthy; the default 1-D minimizer in most libraries. Its accuracy is 2(rtol·|x| + xtol/3), so far from 0 the relative part rtol·|x| dominates xtol.
references: Brent (1973), Algorithms for Minimization without Derivatives, Ch. 5 (localmin)
Forsythe, Malcolm & Moler (1977), Computer Methods for Mathematical Computations, fmin
Press et al., Numerical Recipes (3rd ed.), §10.3 (routine Brent)

name: Dichotomous search

params.name: xtol
params.help: Stop when the bracket width b − a ≤ xtol; then |x − x⋆| ≤ max(xtol, h) for unimodal f, with h ≈ √ε·(1 + |x⋆|). A small δ = delta_ratio·xtol can make rounding decide a comparison first: the run then stops with converged=False.

params.name: delta_ratio
params.help: Separation δ = delta_ratio·xtol of the two points around the midpoint (must be < xtol and < the bracket width b − a). A smaller δ gives smaller f-differences that rounding hides sooner.

params.name: max_iter
params.help: Iteration limit.

summary: Evaluate f just left and right of the midpoint and keep the half that contains the lower value; the bracket almost halves each step.
references: Bazaraa, Sherali & Shetty, Nonlinear Programming (3rd ed.), §8.2 (dichotomous search)

name: Fibonacci search

params.name: xtol
params.help: Stop when the bracket width b − a ≤ xtol. For unimodal f, |x − x⋆| ≤ max(xtol, h): f-comparisons cannot resolve x⋆ below h ≈ √ε·(1 + |x⋆|) (about 10⁻⁸).

params.name: eps_ratio
params.help: Shift ε of the last step as a fraction of the final Fibonacci interval (b₀ − a₀)/Fₙ.

params.name: max_iter
params.help: Iteration limit.

order: linear (optimal for a fixed number of evaluations)
summary: Plan n evaluations in advance so the final interval is as small as possible; points sit at Fibonacci ratios and each step reuses one old point.
references: Kiefer (1953), Sequential minimax search for a maximum, Proc. AMS 4, 502–506
Bazaraa, Sherali & Shetty, Nonlinear Programming (3rd ed.), §8.2 (Fibonacci search)
Luenberger & Ye, Linear and Nonlinear Programming (4th ed.), Ch. 8 (Fibonacci and golden section search)

name: Golden-section search

params.name: xtol
params.help: Stop when the bracket width b − a ≤ xtol. For unimodal f, |x − x⋆| ≤ max(xtol, h): f-comparisons cannot resolve x⋆ below h ≈ √ε·(1 + |x⋆|) (about 10⁻⁸).

params.name: max_iter
params.help: Iteration limit.

summary: Compare f at two golden-ratio points, discard the worse end; one of the old points is reused, so each step costs one new evaluation.
references: Kiefer (1953), Sequential minimax search for a maximum, Proc. AMS 4, 502–506
Press et al., Numerical Recipes (3rd ed.), §10.2 (routine Golden)
Bazaraa, Sherali & Shetty, Nonlinear Programming (3rd ed.), §8.2

name: Newton's method (1-D minimization)

params.name: gtol
params.help: Stop when |f′(x)| ≤ gtol and f″(x) ≥ 0 (necessary conditions only: x can be an inflection point).

params.name: alpha0
params.help: First trial length of the gradient step used when f″(x) ≤ 0.

params.name: max_iter
params.help: Iteration limit.

order: quadratic near a minimizer with f″ > 0
summary: Jump to the minimizer of the local quadratic model x − f′/f″; when the model is not convex (f″ ≤ 0), take a backtracking gradient step instead.
references: Nocedal & Wright, Numerical Optimization (2nd ed.), §3.3 (Newton) and Alg. 3.1 (backtracking)
Luenberger & Ye, Linear and Nonlinear Programming (4th ed.), Ch. 8 (Newton's method for line search)

name: Successive parabolic interpolation

params.name: xtol
params.help: Stop when xₘ is within xtol/2 of both ends of the bracket (so its width ≤ xtol). f-comparisons limit the accuracy to h ≈ √ε·(1 + |x⋆|) (about 10⁻⁸).

params.name: max_iter
params.help: Iteration limit.

order: linear when an end point stays fixed (the unbracketed variant is superlinear, ≈ 1.324)
summary: Fit a parabola through three points that bracket the minimum and jump to its vertex; fall back to golden-section steps when the fit is unusable or makes too little progress, and to bisection until the three points bracket the minimum. The setup evaluates f at both bracket ends, so f must be finite at a and b (choose a bracket inside the domain; Brent's method evaluates interior points only).
references: Press et al., Numerical Recipes (3rd ed.), §10.3, eq. 10.3.1
Brent (1973), Algorithms for Minimization without Derivatives, Ch. 5 (progress test)
Luenberger & Ye, Linear and Nonlinear Programming (4th ed.), Ch. 8 (line search by quadratic fit)
Antoniou & Lu, Practical Optimization (2007), Ch. 4 (quadratic interpolation method)

name: Ternary search

params.name: xtol
params.help: Stop when the bracket width b − a ≤ xtol. For unimodal f, |x − x⋆| ≤ max(xtol, h): f-comparisons cannot resolve x⋆ below h ≈ √ε·(1 + |x⋆|) (about 10⁻⁸).

params.name: max_iter
params.help: Iteration limit.

summary: Split the bracket into thirds, compare f at the two inner points and drop the outer third next to the worse one.
references: Bazaraa, Sherali & Shetty, Nonlinear Programming (3rd ed.), §8.2 (interval elimination)

name: Backtracking (Armijo)

params.help: Search direction p: steepest descent −∇f(x₀) or Newton −∇²f(x₀)⁻¹∇f(x₀).

params.name: alpha0

params.name: c1

params.name: rho
params.help: Contraction factor: α ← ρα.

params.name: max_iter
params.help: Maximum number of trial steps.

summary: Start with a long step and shrink it by ρ until f decreases enough (Armijo).
references: Nocedal & Wright (2006), Numerical Optimization, 2nd ed., Algorithm 3.1 and eq. (3.4)
Armijo (1966), Pacific J. Math. 16

name: Exact step (quadratic model)

params.name: direction
params.help: Search direction p: steepest descent −∇f(x₀) or Newton −∇²f(x₀)⁻¹∇f(x₀).

params.help: Armijo constant c₁: accept only φ(α) ≤ φ(0) + c₁αφ'(0).

summary: Jump straight to the minimizer of the local quadratic model along p.

name: Goldstein (bisection)

params.help: Search direction p: steepest descent −∇f(x₀) or Newton −∇²f(x₀)⁻¹∇f(x₀).

params.name: alpha0

Goldstein (1965), SIAM J. Control 3

name: Weak Wolfe (bisection)

references: Burden & Faires, Numerical Analysis (10th ed.), Theorem 4.4, Alg. 4.1

params.name: n

params.name: tol
params.help: Converged when the final error estimate ≤ tol·max(1, |I|).

summary: Fit a cubic through each group of three subintervals and integrate it exactly.
references: Burden & Faires, Numerical Analysis (10th ed.), §4.3 (closed Newton–Cotes, n = 3)

name: Composite trapezoidal rule

params.name: n

params.name: tol
params.help: Converged when the final error estimate ≤ tol·max(1, |I|).

summary: Join neighboring points with straight lines and add up the trapezoids.
references: Burden & Faires, Numerical Analysis (10th ed.), Theorem 4.5

references: Burden & Faires, Numerical Analysis (10th ed.), §4.1 (h < 0 in Eq. 4.1)

params.name: h0

params.name: levels

params.name: tol
params.help: Converged when the best level's error bound ≤ tol·max(1, |D|).

summary: Slope of the chord from x₀ − h to x₀ + h; the odd error terms cancel.
references: Burden & Faires, Numerical Analysis (10th ed.), Eq. (4.5) (three-point midpoint)

params.name: h0

references: Squire & Trapp, SIAM Review 40 (1998)
Martins, Sturdza & Alonso, ACM TOMS 29 (2003)

params.name: h0

params.name: levels

params.name: tol
params.help: Converged when the best level's error bound ≤ tol·max(1, |D|).

references: Burden & Faires, Numerical Analysis (10th ed.), Eq. (4.6) (five-point midpoint)

params.help: Converged when the best level's error bound ≤ tol·max(1, |D|).

summary: Slope of the secant from x₀ to x₀ + h.
references: Burden & Faires, Numerical Analysis (10th ed.), Eq. (4.1)

params.name: h0
params.help: Largest step; level k uses h₀/2ᵏ.

params.name: levels
params.help: Number of halvings of h (the sweep always runs to the end).

params.name: tol
params.help: Converged when the best level's error bound ≤ tol·max(1, |D|).

summary: Extrapolate central differences on halved steps to h = 0.
references: Burden & Faires, Numerical Analysis (10th ed.), §4.2
Press et al., Numerical Recipes (3rd ed.), §5.7

name: Second derivative (central)

params.name: h0
params.help: Largest step; level k uses h₀/2ᵏ.

params.help: Converged when the best level's error bound ≤ tol·max(1, |D|).

summary: Estimate f″(x₀) from the curvature of three equally spaced points.
references: Burden & Faires, Numerical Analysis (10th ed.), Eq. (4.9)

name: AAA rational approximation

params.name: tol
params.help: Stop when max over the samples of |f − r| ≤ tol·max|f| (NST 2018 default 10⁻¹³).

params.name: max_terms
params.help: Maximum number m of support points; r has type (m − 1, m − 1) (NST 2018 mmax = 100).

params.name: scaling
params.help: 'columns': SVD of the Loewner matrix with unit-norm columns (stable when column norms differ by many orders); 'none': NST 2018 Fig. 4.1 exactly.

order: root-exponential for |x|-type singularities, geometric for analytic f
summary: Add the worst-fit sample as a support point, then choose the barycentric weights that best fit all other samples (smallest singular vector of a Loewner matrix).
references: Nakatsukasa, Sète & Trefethen (2018), The AAA algorithm for rational approximation, SIAM J. Sci. Comput. 40(3): Fig. 4.1 (algorithm), eqs. (3.5)–(3.10) (Loewner least-squares problem), eq. (3.11) (poles), §5 (Froissart doublets)
Schneider & Werner (1986), Some new aspects of rational interpolation, Math. Comp. 47: sign condition on the weights (certified real poles)
van der Sluis (1969), Condition numbers and equilibration of matrices, Numer. Math. 14 (column scaling)

name: Barycentric form
order: error O(hⁿ), n nodes at spacing h: f − p = f⁽ⁿ⁾(ξ)·ω(x)/n!, ω(x) = ∏ⱼ(x − xⱼ)
summary: Precompute one weight per node in O(n²); then evaluate p with a stable O(n) weighted average.
references: Berrut & Trefethen (2004), Barycentric Lagrange Interpolation, SIAM Review 46(3), eq. (3.2) weights, eq. (4.2) second form
Higham (2004), The numerical stability of barycentric Lagrange interpolation, IMA J. Numer. Anal. 24

name: Chebyshev interpolation

params.name: n_nodes
params.help: Number of Chebyshev nodes when the data are samples of f_true (0 = the dataset size). Ignored otherwise (no f_true, or noisy data): the data points are the nodes.

summary: Sample f at the Chebyshev nodes and expand the interpolant in Chebyshev polynomials.
references: Burden & Faires, Numerical Analysis (10th ed.), §8.3 (Chebyshev nodes)
Press et al., Numerical Recipes (3rd ed.), §5.8 (coefficients by discrete orthogonality) and §5.4 (Clenshaw)
Trefethen, Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice (2013), Ch. 3–4

name: Clamped cubic spline

params.name: fprime_a
params.help: Imposed end slope S′(x₀).

params.name: fprime_b
params.help: Imposed end slope S′(xₙ₋₁).

summary: The C² piecewise cubic through the data with prescribed slopes at both ends.
references: de Boor, A Practical Guide to Splines (rev. ed. 2001), Ch. IV (slope form, CUBSPL)
Burden & Faires, Numerical Analysis (10th ed.), §3.5, Theorems 3.11–3.12
Burden & Faires (10th ed.), Alg. 3.5 (same spline, c-form)

name: Natural cubic spline
order: error O(h²) at the ends, O(h⁴) inside
summary: The C² piecewise cubic through the data with zero curvature at both ends.
references: de Boor, A Practical Guide to Splines (rev. ed. 2001), Ch. IV (slope form, CUBSPL)
Burden & Faires, Numerical Analysis (10th ed.), §3.5, Theorems 3.11–3.12
Burden & Faires (10th ed.), Alg. 3.4 (same spline, c-form)

name: Not-a-knot cubic spline
summary: The C² cubic spline whose first two and last two pieces are single cubics.
references: de Boor, A Practical Guide to Splines (rev. ed. 2001), Ch. IV (slope form, CUBSPL)
Burden & Faires, Numerical Analysis (10th ed.), §3.5, Theorems 3.11–3.12

name: Floater–Hormann rational interpolation

params.name: d
params.help: Degree of the blended local interpolants (0 ≤ d ≤ number of nodes − 1); error O(hᵈ⁺¹). d = 0 is Berrut's interpolant; d = n is the polynomial.

summary: Blend the local degree-d interpolants into one rational interpolant: explicit barycentric weights, no real poles, and no Runge oscillation.
references: Floater & Hormann (2007), Barycentric rational interpolation with no poles and high rates of approximation, Numer. Math. 107: eqs. (4), (5) (blend), (11), (18) (weights), Theorem 1 (no real poles), Theorem 2 (O(hᵈ⁺¹))
Berrut & Trefethen (2004), Barycentric Lagrange Interpolation, SIAM Review 46(3), eq. (4.2) (evaluation)

name: Lagrange form
order: error O(hⁿ), n nodes at spacing h: f − p = f⁽ⁿ⁾(ξ)·ω(x)/n!, ω(x) = ∏ⱼ(x − xⱼ)
summary: Write p as Σ y_j ℓ_j, where the basis polynomial ℓ_j is 1 at x_j and 0 at every other node; each evaluation costs O(n²).
references: Burden & Faires, Numerical Analysis (10th ed.), §3.1, Theorem 3.2

name: Linear spline
summary: Join consecutive data points with straight lines.
references: Burden & Faires, Numerical Analysis (10th ed.), §3.5 (piecewise-linear interpolation)

name: Neville's algorithm

params.name: x_frac
params.help: Evaluation point x* = a + x_frac·(b − a) inside the plotting domain [a, b].

order: error O(hⁿ), n nodes at spacing h: f − p = f⁽ⁿ⁾(ξ)·ω(x)/n!, ω(x) = ∏ⱼ(x − xⱼ)
summary: Evaluate p(x*) directly by combining interpolants on ever larger sets of nodes (O(n²) per point).
references: Burden & Faires, Numerical Analysis (10th ed.), §3.2, Alg. 3.1 (Theorem 3.5)

name: Newton divided differences
order: error O(hⁿ), n nodes at spacing h: f − p = f⁽ⁿ⁾(ξ)·ω(x)/n!, ω(x) = ∏ⱼ(x − xⱼ)
summary: Add one node at a time; each new node adds one divided difference and one term (O(n²) table, O(n) per evaluation by nested multiplication).
references: Burden & Faires, Numerical Analysis (10th ed.), §3.3, Alg. 3.2

name: PCHIP (monotone cubic)
summary: A C¹ piecewise cubic whose slopes are chosen so monotone data stay monotone.
references: Fritsch & Carlson (1980), Monotone piecewise cubic interpolation, SIAM J. Numer. Anal. 17(2) (monotonicity region)
Fritsch & Butland (1984), A method for constructing local monotone piecewise cubic interpolants, SIAM J. Sci. Stat. Comput. 5(2) (weighted harmonic mean)
Moler, Numerical Computing with MATLAB (2004), Ch. 3 (pchiptx end slopes)

name: Minimax (Chebyshev) line

params.name: tol
params.help: Stop when max|r| − |h| ≤ tol·max(|h|, ‖y‖∞) + the rounding level of r.

params.name: max_iter
params.help: Exchange limit.

summary: The line that minimizes the largest vertical error; found by exchanging 3 reference points.
references: Stiefel (1959), Über diskrete und lineare Tschebyscheff-Approximationen, Numer. Math. 1 (exchange algorithm)
Cheney, Introduction to Approximation Theory (1966), Ch. 2 (alternation theorem, de la Vallée Poussin ascent)

name: Huber regression (IRLS)

params.name: delta
params.help: Threshold δ in units of σ̂ (1.345 gives 95% efficiency for Gaussian noise).

params.name: tol
params.help: Stop when ‖Δθ‖∞ ≤ tol·(1 + ‖θ‖∞), θ = the line in the centered variable x − x̄.

params.name: max_iter
params.help: IRLS iteration limit.

summary: Quadratic loss for small residuals, linear for large ones; solved by reweighted least squares.
references: Huber (1964), Robust estimation of a location parameter, Ann. Math. Stat. 35
Holland & Welsch (1977), Robust regression using iteratively reweighted least-squares, Commun. Stat. A6
Maronna, Martin & Yohai, Robust Statistics (2006), Ch. 4 (regression M-estimates with a preliminary scale from an L1 fit; IRWLS and its monotone descent)

name: Least absolute deviations (IRLS)

params.name: eps
params.help: Weight floor: w_i = 1/max(|r_i|, eps) (in units of y).

params.name: tol
params.help: Stop when ‖Δθ‖∞ ≤ tol·(1 + ‖θ‖∞), θ = the line in the centered variable x − x̄.

params.name: max_iter
params.help: IRLS iteration limit.

summary: Minimize the sum of absolute residuals by repeatedly solving weighted least squares.
references: Schlossmacher (1973), An iterative technique for absolute deviations curve fitting, JASA 68
Björck, Numerical Methods for Least Squares Problems (1996), Ch. 4 (IRLS for ℓ_p)

name: Linear regression (OLS)

params.name: solver
params.help: QR (stable), normal equations (squares κ), or SVD (rank-revealing).

summary: Fit the line y = β₀ + β₁x that minimizes the sum of squared vertical residuals.
references: Golub & Van Loan, Matrix Computations (4th ed.), §5.3 (Alg. 5.3.1 normal equations, Alg. 5.3.2 Householder LS) and §5.5 (SVD, rank deficiency)
Higham, Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms (2nd ed.), Ch. 20
Montgomery, Peck & Vining, Introduction to Linear Regression Analysis (5th ed.), Ch. 2–3 (standard errors, R², adjusted R²)

name: Polynomial regression

params.name: degree
params.help: Polynomial degree d. With fewer than d + 1 distinct x the fit is not unique: the minimum-norm solution is returned with converged=False.

summary: Least-squares fit of a degree-d polynomial; higher d fits the noise.
references: Golub & Van Loan, Matrix Computations (4th ed.), Alg. 5.3.2 (Householder LS)
van der Sluis (1969), Condition numbers and equilibration of matrices, Numer. Math. 14 (column scaling)

name: Ridge regression

params.name: lam
params.help: Penalty λ on Σ_{j≥1} β_j² (λ = 0, plain OLS, is also accepted).

params.name: degree
params.help: Polynomial degree d.

summary: Least squares plus a penalty λ‖β‖² that shrinks the slope coefficients toward 0.
references: Hastie, Tibshirani & Friedman, The Elements of Statistical Learning (2nd ed.), §3.4.1, eq. (3.41) (intercept not penalized)
Golub & Van Loan, Matrix Computations (4th ed.), §6.1 (Tikhonov regularization as an augmented least-squares problem)

name: Theil–Sen estimator
summary: The slope is the median of the slopes through all pairs of points.
references: Theil (1950), A rank-invariant method of linear and polynomial regression analysis, Indag. Math. 12
Sen (1968), Estimates of the regression coefficient based on Kendall's tau, JASA 63
